children.name: Nothofagus fusca
children.description: Nothofagus fusca, commonly known as red beech (Māori: tawhai raunui) is a species of southern beech, endemic to New Zealand, occurring on both the North and South Island.

children.name: Nothofagus gunnii
children.description: thumb|Nothofagus gunnii in [[Mount Field National Park, showing deciduous autumnal colours.

children.name: Nothofagus solandri
children.description: Nothofagus solandri, commonly known as black beech (Māori: tawai rauriki), is species of tree endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Nothofagus truncata
children.description: Nothofagus truncata, or hard beech ( ), is a species of tree endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Nothofagus cunninghamii
children.description: Nothofagus cunninghamii, commonly known as myrtle beech or Tasmanian myrtle, is the dominant species of cool temperate rainforests in Tasmania and Southern Victoria.

children.name: Nothofagus menziesii
children.description: Nothofagus menziesii, commonly known as silver beech, is a species of evergreen tree in the family Nothofagaceae.

children.name: Nothofagus antarctica
children.description: Nothofagus antarctica (Antarctic beech; in Spanish Ñire or Ñirre) is a deciduous tree or shrub native to southern Chile and Argentina from about 36°S to Tierra del Fuego (56° S), where it grows mainly in the diminishing temperate rainforest.

children.name: Nothofagus betuloides
children.description: Nothofagus betuloides, Magellan's beech or guindo, is a tree native to southern Patagonia.

children.name: Nothofagus dombeyi
children.description: thumb|200px|An ornamental clipboard made of Nothofagus dombeyi heartwood.

children.name: Nothofagus pumilio
children.description: Nothofagus pumilio, the lenga beech that is native to the southern Andes range, in the temperate forests of Chile and Argentina to Tierra del Fuego, from 35° to 56° South latitude.

children.name: Nothofagus alpina
children.description: Nothofagus alpina, also called raulí (in the Mapuche language) or raulí beech, is a species of plant in the Nothofagaceae family.

children.name: Nothofagus obliqua
children.description: Nothofagus obliqua, commonly known as Patagonian oak, roble, pellín, roble pellín, and hualle in its early state of growth or roble beech, is a deciduous tree from Chile and Argentina.

children.name: Nothofagus moorei
children.description: thumb|Large Antarctic beech at Cobark Park, [[Barrington Tops, 50 metres tall]].

children.name: Nothofagus alessandrii
children.description: Nothofagus alessandrii, commonly known as the ruil, is a species of plant in the family Nothofagaceae, it is also known as the southern beeches.
